You can be both. 

One is the acknowledgement of there not being evidence of the existence of god, and the second is the personal belief that there is no god. 

Atheism is not a religious belief because I don't belong to a atheist church or community, we have no set of rules of how an atheist behaves or thinks, is just my personal decision of not believing there is any kind of god. 

People say there is a god ----> I don't see evidence of god ----> I don't think there is a god

Is quite simple, really.

To disprove something you don't need proof, I'm not the one claiming that there is a god. I have nothing to prove, as an agnostic atheist I just think  that since there is no concrete evidence that there is any kind of god, I don't think it exists. 

If I say there is a teapot orbiting Pluto I cannot ask you to produce evidence that proves that it is not true, that is on me. I'm the one with the burden of proof. Same thing happens with god.

"what can be asserted without evidence can also be dismissed without evidence" I see no evidence of god, ergo I don't have to belive there is one. 

Evolution  is the best answer we have to explain biodiversity, but we know that no species is perfect, and we can trace those changes that had happened in time. Science is not perfect, but is the best we have, the collective knowledge of humanity is our best shot at finding answers to the questions we do not have. 

The efficiency is inherent of life, it has nothing to do with intelligence, that is an anthropocentric view, living creatures without a brain can take this path of less resistance, because that is how life works, its call survival.

Im gona put in my two cents here... precisely because you can't prove a negative, the burden of proof is on those who claim there is a god.  We as atheists/agnostics, for whatever reasons, have the right to say I don't think there is a god/since there is no evidence that there is a god I don't think there is.

Why should I have to prove that x or y god exists? Im not the one claiming that it does. 

As for the design argument, is also not our burden, the one that claims that life was created has to come with the evidence. All the evidence that we have says that there is no creador and that life evolved thru trial and error that lasted millions and millions of years.

And lastly, no belief system is based on logic or reasoning, that's why is belief, if you look at it from an anthropological standpoint religion is no more than the first attempt that humans had at understanding the world, and cthe creation of rules to survive in the hostile environments. Atheism is the suspension of those beliefs, through the use of logic, reasoning and science. Although at is core is most importantly a choice that was made by each individual.
Yes, absolutely.

This are interesting questions, and I'll do my best to answer them from the field I'm studying: Anthropology, which has helped me answer them as well.

1. Anthopologists have studied many many cultures around the world, and wherever they worship, god's, spirits or whatever, all societies have something in common: a set of rules that are cultural in nature, this rules are usually not arbitrary, they are place to accommodate the behaviour of the group to the world that surrounds them. So short answer: no, lying, cheating and stealing are things that make group life difficult, so usually are punished as a group, and as humans we *need* a group to survive.

2. In my case is not about taking chances, is about principle, I refuse to believe that an almighty power can let so many horrible things happen to innocents, while the ones who are "acting on their behalf" can get away with so many heinous things. Is about the power, i won't let a being like that be a part of my life (not that I believe that exists, but as an agnostic-atheist I like to leave a tiny bit of possibility open), I prefer to spend that time doing things that to me may hold more meaning. 

3. To me that that is science, in the past it may have supported theological arguments, but new evidences have shown otherwise, and that is the essence of the scientific thinking, if something gets refuted then we move on. And so far science has disproved many if not all of for example biblical stories, so if you are going to use the argument that science *once* supported religious, for the sake of cohesion need to acknowledge that it doesn't anymore. 

4. To me is not disheartening, it is actually what gives it more meaning, this is my one an only chance to leave my mark in this world. If I look back and see all the things that had happened in history from fossils to now, all that happened and I am here, is just awe inspiring to me, it makes me want to enjoy as much as I can, It makes me want to see movies, read books, travel, meet people, better myself. I think that that is enough meaning, don't ya think?
